segments.text: CHAPTER 3 Blockchain-Based Privacy-Preserving Authentication Framework Using Hybrid Adaptive Network for Internet of Vehicles 3.1 Preamble
segments.label: human

segments.text: The rapid growth of intelligent transportation systems has led to the development of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), where vehicles, roadside units, and cloud servers communicate continuously to support applications such as traffic safety, autonomous driving, and real-time navigation. While IoV improves transportation efficiency and user experience, it also introduces serious security and privacy challenges due to its open wireless environment, high vehicle mobility, and large-scale data exchange. Traditional centralized authentication mechanisms depend on trusted authorities, which suffer from scalability issues, high latency, and single-point-of-failure problems, making them unsuitable for dynamic IoV scenarios. Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution by enabling decentralized, tamper-resistant, and transparent authentication without relying on a central entity. However, blockchain alone cannot effectively handle intelligent and evolving cyber-attacks such as impersonation and false data injection. To overcome this limitation, intelligent learning models are required to detect malicious behavior accurately. In this context, this chapter presents an efficient privacy-preserving authentication scheme that integrates blockchain technology with a Hybrid Adaptive Network (HANet) to provide secure, scalable, and intelligent authentication in IoV networks. The proposed framework ensures data integrity, vehicle anonymity, and resistance to malicious attacks while maintaining low computational overhead, thereby making it suitable for real-time vehicular environments.

segments.text: 3.2 Background and Motivation​
segments.label: human

segments.text: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) represents a large-scale, heterogeneous communication environment where vehicles, roadside units (RSUs), infrastructure, and users exchange information through wireless networks to enable intelligent transportation services. This interconnected ecosystem supports applications such as traffic
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: monitoring, accident prevention, and autonomous driving. With the advancement of machine learning and deep learning techniques, data collected by RSUs and vehicles can be effectively utilized to build intelligent systems for vehicular misbehavior detection, trust evaluation, and anomaly identification, as highlighted by Kumar et al. (2022) and Wang et al. (2022). However, traditional machine learning techniques often struggle to operate efficiently in highly distributed and dynamic IoV environments due to limited adaptability and generalization issues. Security and privacy remain major concerns in IoV networks because vehicles continuously transmit sensitive information such as location, identity, and driving patterns. Conventional IoV security solutions are primarily centralized and rely on trusted authorities, which introduce single-point-of-failure problems and scalability limitations, as discussed by Wang et al. (2019) and Qureshi et al. (2022). These centralized approaches are vulnerable to attacks such as unauthorized tracking, identity hijacking, replay attacks, and the injection of false information, which can mislead vehicles and compromise road safety. Moreover, centralized trust models may fail to provide timely authentication and accountability in high-mobility vehicular environments. Another critical challenge is ensuring conditional privacy, where vehicles remain anonymous during normal operation but can be traced and penalized when malicious behavior is detected. Existing trust-based approaches typically depend on third-party authorities to validate transactions, which may themselves become untrustworthy or compromised, as highlighted by Mundhe et al. (2022) and Chaudhary and Singh (2021). As IoV networks grow in scale and complexity, traditional security mechanisms become insufficient due to ineffective malicious node traceability, insecure communication channels, and inefficient data transmission mechanisms. Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution to address these challenges by enabling decentralized, tamper-resistant, and transparent data management. Blockchain distributes trust among participating nodes using consensus
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: mechanisms, eliminating the need for centralized authorities, as demonstrated by Wang et al. (2019), Chai et al. (2022), and Feng et al. (2022). In a blockchain-based IoV environment, transactions are recorded through a peer-to-peer network, and each node maintains a synchronized copy of the distributed ledger. Before any transaction is permanently stored, it is validated by multiple nodes, ensuring data integrity and transparency. The immutability property of blockchain ensures that any modification to stored data is computationally infeasible, thereby strengthening resistance against data tampering and insider attacks. Despite these advantages, blockchain-based IoV systems may suffer from communication overhead, storage consumption, and latency issues, particularly when handling large volumes of vehicular data. Federated Learning (FL) has been proposed as an effective solution to mitigate these limitations by allowing vehicles to train local models without sharing raw data, as demonstrated by Lu et al. (2020), Fan et al. (2022), and Wang et al. (2022). FL enhances privacy preservation and reduces network congestion while enabling collaborative learning. However, FL-based IoV systems are still vulnerable to malicious model updates, inference attacks, and inefficient aggregation processes. Machine learning techniques provide intelligent solutions for analyzing large-scale IoV data and identifying abnormal traffic patterns. Hybrid learning models are particularly effective in distinguishing malicious and normal traffic behavior due to their ability to capture complex data patterns, as discussed by Ali et al. (2021) and Nie et al. (2020). Motivated by these observations, this research integrates blockchain technology with a hybrid adaptive machine learning model to ensure secure, efficient, and privacy-preserving authentication in IoV networks. The proposed framework combines smart contract–enabled blockchain with an intelligent Hybrid Adaptive Network (HANet) to detect malicious activities, secure data transmission, reduce latency, and optimize resource utilization in dynamic vehicular environments. The key contributions of the proposed privacy-preserving authentication scheme for Internet of Vehicles are summarized as follows:

This dynamic nature significantly increases the complexity of data processing, communication reliability, and service continuity. As a result, IoV networks are more vulnerable to security and privacy threats such as sensitive data exposure, identity impersonation, message forgery, and data manipulation, which may directly endanger passenger safety and property. Blockchain technology offers an effective solution to these challenges by enabling decentralized trust management through distributed consensus mechanisms. segments.label: human

segments.text: Blockchain technology, first introduced as the core mechanism behind Bitcoin in 2008, represents a decentralized and autonomous framework for managing and validating time-stamped transactions without reliance on a central authority. It operates as a peer-to-peer (P2P) distributed network in which all participating nodes maintain identical copies of a shared ledger, ensuring consistency and resilience against data tampering. As highlighted by X. Wang et al. (2019) and K. N. Qureshi et al. (2022), blockchain integrates multiple advanced technologies, including asymmetric cryptography, distributed ledger management, smart contracts, and incentive mechanisms, to establish trust in open and untrusted environments such as the Internet of Vehicles (IoV).
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: In a blockchain network, user identities are typically represented through cryptographic public keys, which provide anonymity while preserving authentication and accountability. Transaction data are organized into fundamental units known as blocks, each of which is cryptographically linked to its predecessor, forming an immutable chain. Once a block is validated and appended to the ledger through a consensus process, its contents cannot be altered without modifying all subsequent blocks, a task that is computationally infeasible. This property ensures data integrity, transparency, and traceability, as emphasized by H. Chai et al. (2022) and Xia Feng et al. (2022). Depending on access control and management strategies, blockchains can be broadly categorized into public chains, consortium (permissioned) chains, and private chains, each differing in trust assumptions, consensus mechanisms, and degrees of decentralization. Despite these variations, core blockchain characteristics—such as immutability, encryption, chronological data ordering, openness, and auditability—remain consistent across implementations. Structurally, blockchain systems are commonly organized into layered architectures comprising the data layer, network layer, consensus layer, incentive layer, contract layer, and application layer, as discussed by Chen Mao et al. (2021). This layered infrastructure enables blockchain to support secure, scalable, and privacy-aware applications, making it particularly suitable for authentication and data management in IoV environments.

segments.text: A detailed examination of existing optimization techniques reveals that, although many algorithms demonstrate acceptable performance, they often suffer from limitations related to slow convergence and an improper balance between exploration and exploitation. In large-scale learning environments, some methods also become unstable when handling limited or imbalanced training samples, which can indirectly compromise data privacy and model reliability. To overcome these challenges, nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithms have gained attention due to their adaptability and computational efficiency. Among them, the Beluga Whale Optimization (BWO) algorithm has shown strong capability in addressing both unimodal and multimodal optimization problems with relatively low computational cost. The BWO algorithm is inspired by the natural behaviors of beluga whales, marine mammals well known for their advanced communication and coordinated movement patterns. By simulating these behaviors, the original BWO algorithm has been successfully applied to various optimization tasks and has demonstrated competitive performance compared to other metaheuristic approaches. However, the conventional BWO relies on random selection strategies during population initialization and update phases, which can lead to suboptimal convergence and reduced solution accuracy, particularly in complex and high-dimensional problem spaces.

segments.text: To address these shortcomings, an enhanced version referred to as Opposition Beluga Whale Optimization (OBWO) is introduced. The OBWO algorithm incorporates opposition-based learning principles to improve population diversity and guide the search process more effectively toward optimal regions. This enhancement enables the algorithm to better capture complex structural relationships in the learning space and strengthens the propagation of relevant features within the model. As a result, the OBWO-driven parameter tuning process improves convergence speed while minimizing the objective cost function. In the proposed privacy-preserving authentication framework for IoV, OBWO is employed to optimally tune model parameters, thereby enhancing authentication accuracy and system robustness. The improved convergence behavior and scalability of OBWO contribute to reliable performance even in dynamic and large-scale vehicular environments. segments.text: Authentication plays a vital role in ensuring that vehicular data are accessed, shared, and stored in a secure and trustworthy manner within Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments. To strengthen authentication while preserving user privacy, this research integrates intelligent learning techniques with smart contract–enabled blockchain mechanisms. In particular, a Hybrid Adaptive Network (HANet) is developed by combining a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model with a Ridge classifier to achieve reliable and efficient authentication. The
segments.label: ai_generated

Recent advancements in deep learning have enabled more robust security solutions by facilitating intelligent decision-making over large-scale and dynamic data. Such models have been increasingly adopted to improve privacy protection and authentication in complex networked systems. Nevertheless, many existing deep learning approaches suffer from high training complexity, long convergence time, and susceptibility to overfitting, which limit their practical applicability in real-time IoV scenarios. For instance, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), although effective in feature extraction, often fail to capture long-term dependency patterns and introduce additional computational overhead. To overcome these challenges, this research adopts an MLP–Ridge hybrid framework. The MLP model ensures fast learning and rapid prediction by efficiently capturing nonlinear relationships within vehicular traffic data, whereas the Ridge classifier provides regularization to control overfitting and improve generalization performance. By integrating these complementary models, the proposed HANet achieves a balanced trade-off between learning efficiency, classification robustness, and computational cost, making it well suited for secure and privacy-preserving authentication in IoV networks.

segments.text: 3.5.3 Machine Learning-Based Authentication Using Smart Contracts​
segments.label: human

segments.text: Internet of Vehicles environments are exposed to a wide range of security threats, including cyber intrusions, Sybil attacks, and the participation of compromised or malicious entities, which seriously affect the reliability of vehicular communications. Prior studies have emphasized that traditional rule-based and cryptographic security mechanisms alone are insufficient to handle such intelligent and evolving attacks in IoV networks (Ali et al., 2021). As a result, intelligent data-driven techniques have gained attention for strengthening authentication and attack detection. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool in this context, as it enables systems to learn complex patterns from data and identify abnormal behaviors with high accuracy. Recent research has shown that integrating machine learning with blockchain can significantly improve the security and trustworthiness of distributed systems (Kumar et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022). Blockchain provides an immutable and decentralized ledger, while machine learning enhances decision-making by analyzing transaction behaviors and network traffic. When combined with smart contracts, this integration enables automated, tamper-resistant, and secure validation of vehicular transactions without relying on centralized authorities. However, existing approaches still face limitations in terms of detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and adaptability to large-scale IoV environments.
segments.label: ai_generated

segments.text: To address these challenges, this research proposes a Hybrid Adaptive Network (HANet) for malicious activity detection and authentication in blockchain-enabled IoV systems. The HANet model integrates a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) with a Ridge classifier to leverage the strengths of both learning paradigms. The MLP component effectively captures nonlinear and complex patterns in vehicular data, while the Ridge classifier mitigates overfitting and handles correlated features, as highlighted in earlier machine learning studies (Yadav and Vijayakumar, 2022). Through this hybrid design, every transaction in the IoV network is verified and authenticated before being recorded on the blockchain via smart contracts. During the training phase, the proposed HANet learns to distinguish between legitimate and malicious behaviors, enabling early detection of unauthorized access attempts. The model is capable of processing large volumes of vehicular data efficiently, which is essential for real-time IoV applications. To further enhance performance, key network parameters are optimally tuned using the proposed Opposition Beluga Whale Optimization (OBWO) algorithm, inspired by the work of Zhong et al. (2022).
